newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH PARLIAMENT COMMITTEE EMU RULING DUE JUN 11.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH PARLIAMENT COMMITTEE EMU RULING DUE JUN 11.

text.p: Parliament's constitutional committee plans to complete on June 11 its ruling on the procedure for the legislature's vote on Finnish EMU membership, a parliament official said on Thursday.
"The ruling will be ready next week's Wednesday in the morning," the committee's secretary Jarmo Vuorinen told Reuters by telephone.
The committee had planned to announce its verdict today, but decided it still needed more time, he said, declining to elaborate.
The constitutional committee's decision, which cannot be overruled, will determine the legislative procedure for the vote on membership of European economic and monetary union.
Vuorinen declined comment when asked which way the committee was leaning. Media reports have said the verdict is likely to be along the lines hoped for by the pro-EMU government coalition.
The government has said it intends to give early next year a notification to parliament on the issue of EMU membership. It thinks parliament can vote by simple majority for or against.
With the notification procedure, the vote would also be a measure of parliament's confidence in the government.
The notification procedure goes against the five-party left-right-green coalition's own programme, which says the EMU membership issue would be given to parliament as a proposal to become law.
If handled according to the regular legislation process, a proposal on EMU membership could be delayed in parliament by a variety of formalities and technicalities.

The opposition Centre Party led by ex-PM Esko Aho -- whose centre-right coalition upon taking Finland into the European Union in 1995 promised that parliament would have the chance to vote on joining EMU -- has demanded a law proposal.
The opposition also thinks that the vote on EMU membership should require constitutional order, meaning that two thirds of MPs must support joining the single currency.
The government parties have 141 seats in the 200-seat single-chamber legislature.
The finance ministry is scheduled to hold on June 11 at 1000/0700 GMT a background briefing for journalists on the status of Finland's EMU preparations.
